newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson in tattered pants says he's broke.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson in tattered pants says he's broke.

text.p: O.J. Simpson, wearing ragged pants with a hole in the back, said on Friday he had no money and would have to move out of his mansion because of the wrongful-death damage award against him.
"I know I'm broke. I know I'm retired," the ex-football star told reporters after a second day of discussions with lawyers trying to collect $33.5 million from him.
Asked if he would move from his mansion in an exclusive section of Los Angeles, Simpson replied: "Anyplace that's home -- it's emotional a little bit, but I'm prepared to move."
In contrast, a lawyer for the murder victims' families told reporters Simpson was not as broke as he was saying.

"I should be so flat broke!" Gary Caris, who represents murder victim Ronald Goldman's father Fred said. He added Simpson had earned $400,000 since the beginning of the year, from business deals, pension funds and signing autographs.

Simpson was found not guilty by a criminal jury in 1995 of the June 12, 1994, killings of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and Goldman, but was found liable for their deaths earlier this year in a civil case.
On Thursday and Friday lawyers for the plaintiffs met with Simpson and his lawyers to ask him about his assets. The meeting adjourned Friday and will continue on June 27.
"It was more productive for both sides (on Friday) because Mr. Petrocelli was not there," said Simpson, referring to Goldman's main lawyer, Daniel Petrocelli.
Thursday's proceedings were acrimonious, with Petrocelli complaining about Simpson's "complete lack of candor" in discussing his financial affairs.

Petrocelli also complained that Simpson's attorney, Ronald Slates, was attempting to obstruct his questioning and that Simpson and Slates were refusing to hand over Simpson's cancelled checks and bank records.
But Caris said he was happy with the information handed over on Friday. "Between the documents we received and Mr. Simpson's testimony, I think we made a lot of headway."
But he said Simpson seemed to be favouring paying off the Brown family, since that money went to his ex-wife's estate -- the two children he had with her who now live with him.
"Ultimately he thinks that will enable the money to flow back to himself," Caris said. "I'm sure he's not telling the truth."

Following Simpson's civil trial, sheriff's deputies carted away jewelry, furs, silverware and Tiffany lamps and took them to a warehouse where they were being stored pending distribution to the families.

Missing, however, was Simpson's Heisman Trophy, awarded to the best college football player in the nation, and his expensive sports utility vehicle in which he was driven to court by a bodyguard during the civil trial.

Simpson appeared for Friday's hearing wearing slacks with a hole near the back pocket. Notably absent was his wristwatch and jewelry. A source close to the case said he could have been forced to surrender the items had he worn them.
